title: Replace `zlib` with `zlib-ng`

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
[zlib-ng](https://github.com/zlib-ng/zlib-ng) is a replacement for zlib that adds things for "next generation" systems like CPU intrinsics and other optimizations.

I recently ran into it, found out some Linux distros like Fedora and Arch have been replacing zlib with it (as a package named `zlib-ng-compat`), and decided to try replacing Godot's built-in zlib with it.

It is compiled in compatibility mode (`ZLIB_COMPAT`), which effectively acts as a drop-in replacement for the standard zlib instead of a different library that coexists with it (of course, build system needs adjustments) and allows `builtin_zlib` to work as usual.

- x86 in general implements **SSE2** instructions.
- x86_64 adds **SSSE3**, **SSE4.1** and **SSE4.2** on top of that. **AVX2**, **AVX-512** and **(V)PCLMUL** are ignored.
- ARM, both v7 and v8, only adds **NEON**, ignoring **ARMv6** (the only function already has a NEON version) and **CRC32** (too new) instructions.

## Benchmarks

I'm aware DEFLATE and gzip compression algorithms in Godot use zlib, so I experimented with both in a x86_64 machine.

Test project: [compression_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28374046/compression_test.zip)

Build command: `scons -j8 target=editor production=yes`

### Results

Using default compression level in Project Settings. Iterations are in miliseconds. Lower is better.

#### Compress DEFLATE
|Build|1|2|3|4|
|-|-|-|-|-|
|master|1035.08|998.73|991.98|1003.36|
|PR|1029.49|1027.55|1025.84|1031.75|

#### Decompress DEFLATE
|Build|1|2|3|4|
|-|-|-|-|-|
|master|19.06|18.24|18.03|17.97|
|PR|7.42|7.83|7.55|7.5|

#### Compress gzip
|Build|1|2|3|4|
|-|-|-|-|-|
|master|999.07|1003.53|999.20|999.36|
|PR|1033.61|1026.50|1029.05|1035.75|

#### Decompress gzip
|Build|1|2|3|4|
|-|-|-|-|-|
|master|24.24|24.01|24.20|23.55|
|PR|10.39|10.13|10.27|10.10|

On a quick look, we can notice a tiny performance loss during compression (around 1.021-1.03x slower), but a **massive** gain during decompression (around 2.35-2.42x faster). I do believe this is a sacrifice worth making.

## AI disclosure

During some situations where compilation failed, I resorted to AI to find out what defines were correct. Some decisions I took actually go against what it told me to do.

I also asked which ARM optimizations were valid to apply in the `arm` variants, as I'm only familiar that NEON should be applied for both (it suggested to add CRC32 for `arm64`, but I left it out for reasons already mentioned).

Apart from that, no lines have been written by AI.

The script in the test project, however, is mostly AI-generated, with some changes to make it more convenient for usage in a bash script.

Since I had no way to test, I left optimizations for `ppc64` and `loongarch64` out.
